verdict.summary: You can create a HubSpot OAuth app with the CLI and connect accounts right away. The findings mention no review step before installs. HubSpot's manual review only applies if you want a HubSpot Marketplace listing, and listing requires at least 3 active installs from accounts outside your organization. So you get installs first and list afterward.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours to set up the app and connect; 1-3 days more for listing materials (setup guide, policies, demo video) if you want a listing
verdict.approval_wait: None for install-link use. For a Marketplace listing: first review within 10 business days, and the whole feedback cycle is capped at 60 days.

gates.name: OAuth app in your developer account
gates.unlocks: You create the app, get a client ID and secret, and connect your own HubSpot account through Composio.
limits: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes. Refresh them with the refresh token.
Whoever installs must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission in the target account.
Rate limit: 100 requests every 10 seconds per connected account.

gates.name: Private distribution (allowlisted accounts)
gates.unlocks: You can install the app in the specific HubSpot accounts you add to the app's allowlist.
limits: Only accounts on the allowlist can install.
Same 30-minute access-token expiry, installer-permission rule and rate limit as Gate 1.

gates.name: Marketplace distribution (install link; Marketplace listing optional)
gates.unlocks: With marketplace distribution, any HubSpot account can install through your OAuth install URL. A Marketplace listing, which needs HubSpot review, adds discoverability and can later lead to Certification.
limits: Listing requires at least 3 active, unique production installs unaffiliated with you, with app activity in the past 30 days.
You can submit only one app for approval at a time. Others submitted meanwhile are automatically rejected.
Certification requires at least 60 active installs and a >95% API success rate. It is valid for 2 years. If rejected, you must wait 6 months to reapply.
The findings don't say whether unlisted apps have an install cap.
gates.time_to_reach: Install link: same day, no review. Listing: get 3 or more active unaffiliated installs, then about 10 business days for the first review (cycle capped at 60 days). Certification: at least 6 months after listing.

steps.title: Decide whether you need your own app
steps.detail: Composio offers a managed HubSpot OAuth app that works for internal and testing use. Register your own app if you need your own client ID, redirect URI, branding or Marketplace listing.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list is broad and includes Enterprise-only scopes and settings.users.write. Don't copy it as-is.

steps.title: Create a HubSpot developer account
steps.detail: Go to developers.hubspot.com/get-started, click the create developer account button and complete sign-up.
gotchas: The findings don't confirm whether developer features need a paid HubSpot plan.

steps.title: Install the HubSpot CLI and authenticate
steps.detail: Install the HubSpot CLI and run its account authentication command to link it to your developer account. On the current developer platform, you create apps with the CLI.

steps.title: Create the project and choose distribution and auth type
steps.detail: Create a new project with the CLI. Choose OAuth as the auth type. For distribution, choose 'marketplace' if accounts outside your allowlist will install or you plan to list, or 'private' to restrict installs to allowlisted accounts.
gotchas: Apps installed in multiple accounts must use OAuth. Static tokens only suit single-account installs.
Build on a currently supported platform version. Apps on unsupported versions are rejected from listing.

steps.title: Set redirect URL and scopes in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: In app-hsmeta.json, add the Composio callback to redirectUrls. Put only the scopes your agent actually uses in requiredScopes, and put the rest in optionalScopes or conditionallyRequiredScopes. Then upload the project.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Redirect URLs must use https. Plain http is only allowed for localhost, and IP addresses are not accepted.
Enterprise-only scopes will fail for customers on lower plans. Make those scopes optional.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Open the app's Auth page in your developer account and copy the client ID and client secret. In Composio, create a HubSpot auth config that uses your own credentials, and set the same scopes you declared in app-hsmeta.json.
gotchas: Composio's stored token URL uses /oauth/v1/token, but HubSpot documents /oauth/v3/token. Check which one your auth config uses.

steps.title: Connect your own account and check the logs
steps.detail: Run an authorization through Composio with your HubSpot account, signed in as a Super Admin or a user with Marketplace Access. Confirm that tokens are issued and that refresh works. Debug failures under Development > Monitoring > Logs.
gotchas: Access tokens last 30 minutes. Refresh them before they expire rather than waiting for 401 errors.

steps.title: Add test accounts (private) or share the install link (marketplace)
steps.detail: For private distribution, add each customer account to the app's install allowlist. For marketplace distribution, give users your OAuth install URL so they can connect through Composio.

steps.title: Implement uninstall and token handling
steps.detail: Call the Uninstall App API when a user disconnects, and refresh tokens before they expire. Certification requires both, and the demo video must show the uninstall.

steps.title: Prepare listing materials
steps.detail: This step is only needed for a Marketplace listing. Draft a public setup guide, support URLs, a Terms of Service URL and a Privacy Policy URL. Write pricing that matches your website and Shared data entries that match your scopes. Provide an install button URL and at least one support contact. Allowlist the 'HubSpot Crawler' user agent so HubSpot can verify the URLs.
gotchas: All URLs must be public and under 250 characters.
Remove any scope the app doesn't use.
Classic CRM cards are not allowed in listed apps.

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Record a demo that shows the app working. It must show a user disconnecting, the Uninstall App API being called, and the app disappearing from Connected Apps. Since March 31, 2026, demo materials replace test credentials.

steps.title: Reach 3 active installs, accept the agreement and submit
steps.detail: Once at least 3 unaffiliated production accounts have shown app activity in the last 30 days, accept the Technology Partner Program Agreement and submit the listing. Listing and certification are free, with no revenue share.
gotchas: Submit only one app at a time. Other submissions are automatically rejected while one is in review.

steps.title: Wait for Ecosystem Quality review
steps.detail: HubSpot's Ecosystem Quality team reviews the listing manually. Expect a first response within 10 business days. The total feedback cycle is capped at 60 days.

requirements.detail: Create it from the developer portal.
Register it in redirectUrls or on the Auth page. It must be https (http only for localhost) and cannot be an IP address.
Whoever installs must be a Super Admin or have HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.

requirements.item: OAuth as the sole auth method, with marketplace distribution
requirements.detail: Required for a Marketplace listing, along with a single public app ID matching the OAuth client ID.
Unique production accounts with OAuth API activity or signed webhook/card activity in the past 30 days.
Setup guide, support, Terms of Service and Privacy Policy URLs, plus pricing, Shared data, install button URL and a support contact.
Must show the user disconnecting, the Uninstall App API being called, and the app disappearing from Connected Apps.
Must be accepted. The app must not be in a restricted industry.
Apps on versions HubSpot has declared unsupported are rejected. New versions ship twice a year.

scopes.effect: HubSpot adds it to every app automatically.
Standard CRM access. Some sensitive variants require Enterprise accounts.
Only available on Enterprise accounts. Make them optional so installs on lower tiers don't fail.
Included in Composio's defaults. Leave it out unless you need it, because listing requires removing unused scopes.
Some need Professional or Enterprise plans. HubSpot has no separate review for restricted scopes, but listing review checks that every scope is used.

blockers.symptom: Listing submission rejected or not accepted for review
blockers.cause: Fewer than 3 active unaffiliated installs, or no demo video.
blockers.fix: Get real customer installs through your install link first. Then record the required demo video.

blockers.cause: HubSpot's crawler can't reach your setup guide or policy URLs.
blockers.fix: Make the URLs public and under 250 characters, and allowlist the 'HubSpot Crawler' user agent.

blockers.cause: Only one app can be in review at a time.
blockers.fix: Wait for the current review to finish before submitting another app.

blockers.cause: The installer lacks Super Admin or Marketplace Access permission, or a required scope needs a higher HubSpot plan.
blockers.fix: Ask an admin to install. Move tier-gated scopes to optional.

blockers.cause: The refresh token is invalid, expired or revoked.
blockers.fix: Have the user re-authorize. Refresh access tokens before their 30-minute expiry.

blockers.symptom: Can't create a legacy public app
blockers.cause: A community source reports that legacy public app creation was sunset on June 23, 2026.
blockers.fix: Create the app on the current developer platform with the CLI.

composio.note: Composio's managed HubSpot app is fine for internal use and testing. Register your own app when you need your own client ID, redirect URI, branding or a Marketplace listing. Don't copy Composio's default scopes into your own app: they include Enterprise-only scopes and settings.users.write, and listing requires removing unused scopes. Composio's stored token URL is /oauth/v1/token, while HubSpot documents /oauth/v3/token. Confirm which one your auth config uses, and register the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

evidence.claim: Composio's HubSpot toolkit reports a managed OAUTH2 auth config with HubSpot's authorize and token URLs and a default Composio redirect URI.
flags: no probe was run against this host

evidence.claim: The HubSpot developer account is created from the developer portal; the get-started page has a 'create developer account' call to action and no login wall.
Apps are created with the HubSpot CLI; distribution (marketplace or private) and auth type (OAuth or static token) are chosen during setup.
Distribution is marketplace (eligible for listing) or private (allowlist of accounts); multi-account apps must use OAuth.
Client ID, secret and redirect URLs are on the app's Auth page; app-hsmeta.json lists redirectUrls, requiredScopes, optionalScopes and conditionallyRequiredScopes.
The authorization URL is https://app.hubspot.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, scope and redirect_uri parameters.
The code exchange is a form-encoded POST to /oauth/v3/token returning access_token, refresh_token, hub_id, scopes and expires_in.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes; the refresh token is used with grant_type refresh_token at the v3 token endpoint.
Refresh-token expiry is not stated; invalid, expired or revoked refresh tokens return invalid_grant.
Redirect URIs must be registered and use https in production (http only for localhost); IP addresses are not accepted.
The 'oauth' scope is added by default; scopes are required, conditionally required or optional, and users can decline optional scopes.
Many scopes are tier-gated to Enterprise, Professional or Enterprise plans.
There is no separate restricted scope class with its own review; review checks that every requested scope is used.
Installers must be a Super Admin or hold HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
Listing requires a single public app ID, OAuth only, at least three active unique installs, minimal scopes, the Technology Partner Program Agreement, and a non-restricted industry.
Active installs are unaffiliated production accounts with app activity in the past 30 days.
Listings need a public setup guide, support, ToS and Privacy URLs, pricing, Shared data, install button URL and a support contact; URLs must be public and under 250 characters.
HubSpot recommends allowlisting the 'HubSpot Crawler' user agent before submission.
The Ecosystem Quality team reviews listings manually, with initial review within 10 business days and the cycle capped at 60 days.
Only one app can be submitted at a time; others are automatically rejected.
A demo video showing disconnect, the Uninstall App API call and removal from Connected Apps is required.
Test credentials are no longer required as of March 31, 2026; demo materials replace them.
Apps must run on a supported platform and API version; new versions ship twice a year.
Classic CRM cards are not allowed in listed apps.
Certification requires 6+ months listed, 60+ active installs, >95% API success and respecting the rate limit.
Certification review responds within 10 business days; rejected apps may reapply after six months.
Certification is valid for two years; HubSpot can unpublish apps at any time.
Rate limit is 100 requests per 10 seconds per connected account; no lower cap for new apps was found.
Apps must use the Uninstall App API and refresh tokens before expiry.
There is no fee to list or certify and no revenue share.
Legacy public app creation is reported as sunset on June 23, 2026 (community report, unconfirmed officially).
OAuth install events are viewable under Development > Monitoring > Logs.
The HubSpot authorize endpoint is live and returned a 200 OAuth page.

open_questions: Whether a paid HubSpot plan is needed for developer features is unverified.
Refresh-token lifetime and rotation behavior are not documented in the pages read.
Which Composio callback to register (/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback or /api/v1/auth-apps/add). Use the one shown in your auth config.
Whether unlisted marketplace-distribution apps have an install cap before review is unverified.
The legacy public-app sunset date (June 23, 2026) comes only from a community source.
